title_affiliation: Associate Professor, The George Washington University
biography:
John Paul (JP) is an Associate Professor at George Washington University
in the Department of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering. His
research focuses on understanding how consumer preferences, market
dynamics, and policy affect the emergence and adoption of low-carbon
technologies, such as electric vehicles and renewable energy
technologies. He also studies the critical relationship between the US
and China in developing and mass producing these technologies. He has
expertise in exploratory data analysis, data visualization, reproducible
workflows, choice modeling, conjoint analysis, survey design,
interview-based research methods, the R programming language, China, and
the global electric vehicle industry. He speaks fluent Mandarin Chinese
and has conducted extensive fieldwork in China. John holds a Ph.D. and
M.S. in Engineering and Public Policy from Carnegie Mellon University
and a B.S. in Engineering Science and Mechanics (ESM) from Virginia
Tech.

Lead Data Scientist specializing in product analytics, experimentation

title_affiliation: Professor and Executive Director, American University
biography:
Derrick L. Cogburn is a Full Professor at American University's School
of International Service (SIS), where he is housed in the Department of
Environment, Development & Health. Dr. Cogburn holds a joint appointment
in the Kogod School of Business in the Department of Information
Technology & Analytics. He holds a UNESCO Associate Chair on
Transnational Challenges and Governance and directs both the Institute
on Disability and Public Policy (IDPP) and the Internet Governance Lab
(IGL). He also co-chairs the Global Academic Network for the Center for
AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP).

Dr. Cogburn's research applies computational methods—including text
mining, machine learning, social network analysis, and
retrieval-augmented generation—to international human rights and
disability policy. His current work focuses on UN human rights
monitoring mechanisms, particularly the Universal Periodic Review (UPR)
and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD)
treaty body processes. His applied work includes the CRPD Data
Dashboard, a policy analytics platform developed with IDPP and Praxis
Analytics AI, funded by the National Science Foundation through American
University's Translating Research into Action Center (TRAC). He recently
presented the dashboard at CRPD COSP-19 at the United Nations in New
York, where his side event connected broader human rights accountability
mechanisms to the CRPD treaty framework.

At American University, Dr. Cogburn teaches graduate courses in text
analytics and AI policy, including ITEC/SIS 724: Large-Scale Text
Analysis. In this course, he trains students to become bilingual R and
Python programmers using Positron as their IDE and Quarto documents as
their primary deliverable format. His pedagogical approach integrates
prompt engineering from week two—not as an afterthought—with GitHub
Copilot and Positron Assistant available from day one. He has found that
students without prior programming experience often achieve stronger
bilingual fluency than those who arrive with a single-language
background, a counterintuitive finding that shapes his teaching
philosophy. He has developed a new course for fall 2026 SIS 750 Applied
AI for Global Challenges. 

Dr. Cogburn is currently developing a new graduate certificate at SIS
titled "Global Challenges and Applied AI," anchored by his existing
cross-listed courses and connected to IDPP, IGL, the UNESCO Chair, and
CAIDP. He also runs Praxis Analytics AI, a consulting practice focused
on applied computational social science and AI development for policy
research, small businesses, and non-profit organizations.

Prior to joining American University, Dr. Cogburn held faculty positions
in the Schools of Information at Syracuse University and the University
of Michigan. He is a graduate of Howard University and the University of
Oklahoma.

His professional identity is captured in three words: Scholar. Teacher.
Sailor.

title_affiliation: Head of Partner Solutions Architect AI/ML, Data & Analytics, AWS

biography:
Casey Johnson is a Platform Manager at Pfizer, where he oversees the
strategic direction and operational excellence of the enterprise data
science platforms for Posit. With nearly 10 years of experience, Casey
ensures the stability, scalability, and high performance of Pfizer’s
Posit Workbench, Connect and Package Manager environments, enabling
researchers and data scientists to deploy applications and execute
complex analyses seamlessly.

With a strong background in systems engineering and enterprise
architecture, Casey specializes in navigating the intricacies of
large-scale computational environments. His work focuses on proactively
managing upgrade pathways, optimizing R and Python package dependency
management, and designing robust, secure infrastructure. By aligning
corporate IT standards with agile data science workflows, Casey helps
maintain a reliable foundation that empowers Pfizer’s teams to focus on
delivering life-changing scientific breakthroughs.

Casey enjoys collaborating with peers on best practices for scaling

title_affiliation: Senior Director, Statistical Data Science Analytics, Pfizer
biography:

Pfizer where he has worked for over 30 years. He is also the current
Chair of the R Consortium Board. Mike has had responsibility for looking

colleagues in the Digital IT department to deliver and continue to

she is the data science program lead the company's molecule to treat MPS
IIIA, a pediatric rare disease. As data science program lead, she
oversees all clinical trials related to the molecule and leads the data
science team responsible for generating SDTM, ADaMs, and TLFs for
clinical reporting needs, primarily using R. She holds a Master of
Public Health in Epidemiology and Applied Biostatistics and has spent
six years in the pharma/biotech industry. In addition to her role as
data science program lead, she serves as an R package validation lead,
helping ensure the quality of the R packages used for regulatory
submissions. Nicole is passionate about applying data science and
leveraging open-source tools to accelerate therapies and brings a
practical, cross-functional perspective on the challenges of turning
complex biological data into actionable insight.

engineering, and the implementation of environments to enhance
repeatability and reproducibility in pharmaceutical research. His
expertise has been instrumental in advancing R&D capabilities,

title_affiliation: Clinical Data Specialist, University of Pennsylvania
biography:
Kaitlyn is a clinical data professional with a decade-long career arc
spanning athletic training, clinical research coordination, and applied
data science in academic medical settings. She currently works as a Data
Coordinator in the Neonatology division at Children's Hospital of
Philadelphia (CHOP), where she focuses on leveraging structured and
unstructured EHR data to support pediatric clinical quality improvement.
Kaitlyn also serves as a clinical data specialist at the University of
Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, where she built and
maintained reproducible data pipelines in R, managed clinical trial
data, and developed natural language processing workflows for extracting
clinical meaning from free-text EHR data. Her deep clinical background
shapes how she approaches data problems, grounding computational methods
in the realities of how clinicians document and how care is delivered.
Kaitlyn is passionate about the intersection of clinical expertise and
data science. She holds an MS in Athletic Training, a Data Analytics
Certification from the University of Pennsylvania and completed CHOP's
Data and Analytics University fellowship. Her work has contributed to
publications in critical care and concussion research.

title_affiliation: Data Scientist, National Institutes of Health

quantitative and qualitative analysis. Her work centers on data
integrity at scale — developing protocols to clean and reconcile large
datasets, establishing internal database access with full documentation,
and building dashboards that give leadership a trustworthy, data-driven
view for decision-making.

Kelli holds a Ph.D. in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from the
University of Alabama at Birmingham, where she designed and led

That grounding in experimental rigor now informs her approach to
building trustworthy data pipelines and reporting systems.

title_affiliation: Senior Principal Data Scientist, Bristol Myers Squibb
biography:
Leslie Emery, PhD, is a Senior Principal Data Scientist in the Knowledge
Science Research team at Bristol Myers Squibb working on research for
cancer treatments. She works with a team of translational data
scientists to design and deploy innovative analysis-ready data products
for exploratory research. These data products include custom data
transformation, visualization, & quality tracking apps in R Shiny and
curated & standardized data sets for analysis. She has particular
expertise in harmonizing data from many disparate sources into combined
data sets that enable cross-study or cross-disease analysis. Leslie
works closely with stakeholders from Informatics & Predictive Sciences
and Translational Medicine to define their data and visualization
requirements and deliver them in elegant and efficient ways. Her work
makes it easy for scientists doing drug development research to answer
their scientific questions.

Leslie completed her PhD in genome sciences at the University of
Washington studying the patterns that evolution and population history
have left in current human genetic variation. She then worked as a
Research Scientist at UW Biostatistics on NIH consortium projects
identifying the genetic variants that contribute to common human
diseases. She co-led a team that designed a reproducible python + R
pipeline and SQL database for harmonizing health measurement data for
the TOPMed whole genome sequencing project.

Leslie's many hobbies include knitting, crochet, reading sci-fi, and
tracking and analyzing her hobby data.

Andy Teucher is a core Openscapes team member and develops software and

developer, specializing in helping people and organizations build

title_affiliation: Senior Health Research Analyst, The Ohio State University

biography:
Mirian Lima is a research methodologist working with economic
development data — she packages methods for a living. At the UN Office
of the Special Adviser on Africa, she builds tools that let
non-technical policy analysts run their own code-based analyses — on
numbers they can trust and results they can reproduce. Her work sits at
the seam between rigorous social research methods and modern
computational tooling, exploring how expert judgment can be packaged
into systems that analysts and AI agents can both use well.

title_affiliation: Senior Power Analyst, Seattle City Light

source projects. More recently, Wes has delved into agentic software
engineering with the roborev and msgvault projects, supporting
continuous code review and secure, private email storage and search for

I enjoy partnering across organizations, delivering training, and

title_affiliation: Data Scientist at FNBO (First National Bank of Omaha)
Senior Manager of Data Science, Capital One
biography:
Emily Riederer is a data scientist at Capital One where she leads the
development of specialty underwriting models and serves as a Model Risk
Officer for fraud models. Over the past decade, Emily has worn all the
hats in the data space with work spanning analysis (inference and
measurement), engineering (analyst tools, data pipelines, data
products), and science (core machine learning). She is passionate about
bridging the gaps between these disciplines. While navigating large
enterprise settings, Emily has also served as a “data team of one” for
many pro-bono projects and data-driven voter turnout initiatives.
Outside of work, Emily enjoys supporting open source software and the
free flow of information. She promotes open science by serving on the
editorial board of rOpenSci, on the technical advisory board of
Bluebonnet Data, and as a volunteer statistical textbook reviewer for
Routledge / CRC Press. Her own writing and past talks center on
developing reproducible workflows and exposing the tacit knowledge of
data work and can be found on her website
https://www.emilyriederer.com/.
